==English== ===Alternative forms=== * {{alt|en|lf|LF||specifically "looking for"}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vininn126-look for.wav|a=US}} ===Verb=== {{en-verb|*}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[seek]], to [[try]] to [[find]]. #: {{syn|en|search for}} #: {{ux|en|He spent his life '''looking for''' the truth.}} #: {{ux|en|In July, when classes are over, most college-goers go '''looking for''' jobs.}} #* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=8|passage=The humor of my proposition appealed more strongly to Miss Trevor than I had '''looked for''', and from that time forward she became her old self again; for, even after she had conquered her love for the Celebrity, the mortification of having been jilted by him remained.}} #* {{quote-song|en|author=w:Billy Joel|authorlabel=no|title=w:You May Be Right|album={{w|Glass Houses (album)|Glass Houses}}|date=7 March 1980|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ilsv0C1-aBw|text=You may be right
I may be crazy
Oh, but it just may be a lunatic you're '''looking for'''}} #* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-07-20|volume=408|issue=8845| url=http://www.economist.com/news/asia/21582043-villagers-enjoy-sunlight-after-dark-out-gloom|title=Out of the gloom| passage={{q-g|Rural solar plant}} schemes are of little help to industry or other heavy users of electricity. Nor is solar power yet as cheap as the grid. For all that, the rapid arrival of electric light to Indian villages is long overdue. When the national grid suffers its next huge outage, as it did in July 2012 when hundreds of millions were left in the dark, '''look for''' specks of light in the villages.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130822005257/http://www.economist.com/news/asia/21582043-villagers-enjoy-sunlight-after-dark-out-gloom}} # {{lb|en|transitive|archaic}} To [[expect]]. #: {{syn|en|look after}} ====Derived terms==== {{col2|en|I'm looking for a grocery store|I'm looking for a job |look for a dog to kick |look for trouble |solution looking for a problem}} ====Translations==== {{trans-top|search for; seek}} * Afrikaans: * Albanian: * Altai: * Arabic: * Aragonese: * Armenian: * Asturian: * Azerbaijani: * Bashkir: * Basque: * Belarusian: * Bengali: * Bulgarian: * Burmese: * Catalan: * Chechen: * Cherokee: * Chinese: * Comorian: * Corsican: * Czech: * Danish: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Estonian: * Ewe: * Extremaduran: * Fala: * Faroese: * Finnish: * French: * Friulian: * Galician: * Georgian: * German: * Gothic: * Greek: * Hebrew: * Hindi: * Hmong: * Hungarian: * Icelandic: * Ido: * Indonesian: * Ingrian: * Irish: * Italian: * Japanese: * Kambera: * Kannada: * Kazakh: * Khmer: * Korean: * Kumyk: * Kurdish: * Kyrgyz: * Ladino: * Lao: * Latin: * Latvian: * Leonese: * Lithuanian: * Lombard: * Lü: * Macedonian: * Malay: * Malayalam: * Maltese: * Māori: * Marathi: * Mauritian Creole: * Mirandese: * Mongolian: * Navajo: * Nepali: * Norman: * Norwegian: * Occitan: * Old Church Slavonic: * Old English: * Old Norse: * Pela: * Persian: * Piedmontese: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Quechua: * Romanian: * Romansh: * Russian: {{t+|ru|иска́ть|impf}}, {{t+|ru|поиска́ть|pf}} * Scottish Gaelic: * Serbo-Croatian: * Shor: * Sinhalese: * Slovak: * Slovene: * Sorbian: * Spanish: * Swahili: * Swedish: * Tabaru: * Tajik: * Tamil: * Tatar: * Ternate: * Thai: * Tibetan: * Turkish: * Turkmen: * Ukrainian: * Urdu: * Uyghur: * Uzbek: * Vietnamese: * Welsh: * Yiddish: * Zazaki: * Zhuang: {{trans-bottom}}
